name: Community Rivercare Program

funder.name: Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (Western Australia)

summary: Recurring rounds of small grants for community volunteer groups doing on-ground waterway work in the Swan Canning catchment around Perth: foreshore revegetation, weed control, bank stabilisation and habitat improvement.

steps: Submit additional supporting information, if needed

eligibility.rule: Be incorporated, or be sponsored to administer grant funding
Improve waterway habitat or water quality, revegetate foreshores, control weeds for regeneration, or stabilise banks
Demonstrate a clear public benefit for projects on private land
Work in a waterway or riparian zone in an eligible catchment feeding the Swan and Canning rivers
For revegetation, use local plant species from a NIASA-accredited supplier

documents: Landowner or land manager letter of support (may follow, but needed before approval)
Budget evidence if applicable, including paid contractors’ quotations and ABNs
Sponsor details and agreement evidence, if sponsored
ATO Statement by a supplier form, if applicable

pool.quote: Through Round 10 a total of $100,000 is available to deliver on-ground projects during 2027-28.

applicant_types.quote: Grants of between $3,000 and $10,000 (ex GST) in total for the duration of the project will be provided to community volunteer groups

geography.quote: Projects must be in the Swan Canning Catchment or other catchments that feed into the Swan and Canning rivers.

access.quote: It is strongly recommended that applications are submitted online via the SmartyGrants portal: Community Rivercare Program Round 10.

window.quote: Round 10 Open Monday 26 October 2026 Closing 4pm Friday 11 December 2026

amount.quote: Grants of between $3,000 and $10,000 (ex GST) in total for the duration of the project will be provided to community volunteer groups

effort.quote: Applications close 11 December 2026 (No late applications will be accepted)
All applications will be assessed by a panel consisting of representatives with relevant expertise including foreshore restoration, fauna habitat and water quality.
Any additional or supporting information due* Applicants notified of outcome and negotiations for grant agreements commence 22 January 2027 March 2027

eligibility.quote: Community groups with a volunteer base.

Community groups must be incorporated or sponsored (under an auspicing arrangement) by another group or organisation that will administer their grant funding (see section 13 for more information about sponsorship).

Must address at least one of the following criteria: o habitat improvement for birds and/or other species dependent on waterways; o foreshore revegetation and weed control; o weed control to promote natural regeneration; o bank stabilisation to repair or prevent foreshore erosion; or o water quality improvement.
For projects on private land, a clear benefit to the public must be demonstrated.
Must be in waterways or riparian zones located in the Swan Canning Catchment or other catchments of concern (please contact us for more information) that feed into the Swan and Canning rivers
In 2027-28 between $3,000 and $10,000 (ex GST) is available for one-year projects.
Local plant species must be used. Ensure plants and plant material are sourced from a Nursery Industry Accreditation Scheme Australia (NIASA) accredited supplier.

after_award.quote: A completed report is to be submitted by the grant recipient at the end of each financial year of the project (a reporting template will be supplied by DBCA to the grant recipient).

documents.quote: A letter of support for the project from the land owner(s) or land manager(s) including maintenance commitments and any covenants on the project site. Note: although this may not be available at the time of submission, it is a mandatory requirement prior to funding approval. • Map(s) of the project site clearly showing the location, North arrow and extent of the project.
Timeline for the project identifying when major activities will occur. • Budget clearly detailing what the grant will pay for.

Supporting evidence to justify budget estimates (if applicable). • Applicants with a sponsor (auspicor) will need to provide the sponsoring organisation's details and evidence of their agreement to receive and administer the grant funding. • ATO Statement by a supplier form (if applicable).
Paid contractors undertaking works must provide an ABN and quotation for works proposed.
